Target audience: University students (STEM majors)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Coordinate Systems as Languages

Lecture lines:
Basis vectors form our coordinate language.
Changing basis changes the grid lines.
Positions are defined by relative basis units.

Planned animations:
1. Show coordinate system A in #FFFFFF (white).
2. Transform system A to system B in #00FFFF (cyan).
3. Highlight origin point in #FF00FF (magenta).

Section: section_2 — Defining the Transition Matrix

Lecture lines:
Transition matrix P maps bases.
Columns of P are new basis vectors.
[v]_B = P * [v]_B' relates coordinates.

Planned animations:
1. Draw vectors v_A and v_B in #FFFFFF.
2. Highlight basis vectors of system A in #FFFF00 (yellow).
3. Show projection of v_A onto B basis in #00FF00 (green).

Section: section_3 — The Mechanism: How to Calculate

Lecture lines:
Step 1: Identify your basis vectors.
Step 2: Place them as columns in P.
Step 3: Multiply P by coordinate vector.

Planned animations:
1. Display matrix M in #FFFFFF.
2. Visualize multiplication of basis vector i_A by M in #00FFFF.
3. Complete transformation of unit square grid in #FF8000 (orange).

Section: section_4 — Summary & Geometric Intuition

Lecture lines:
Change of basis is space relabelling.
The vector itself stays the same.
P-inverse converts back to original basis.

Planned animations:
1. Show superposition of original and transformed grids in #FFFFFF.
2. Highlight vector v_A as stationary in #FFFF00.
3. Illustrate v_B as the result of M * v_A in #00FF00.

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
